title: Agent, MCP and skill attacks

atom_notes.A16: the model reads tool descriptions, retrieved text and skill files as instructions
atom_notes.A02: the agent's permissions become the attacker's permissions once a tool call is induced
atom_notes.A11: an MCP server or skill is a dependency that is trusted and rarely reviewed
atom_notes.A08: tool output and memory carry data across sessions and users

required_cells.why: inventory every MCP server, skill and tool the agent can call
probe descriptions and registries, not just inputs
induce a tool call and observe the effect, that is the exploit
prove the effect with a control input that must not trigger it
pin and verify tool descriptions, the supply chain fix
detect new or changed tools in the registry

entries.name: MCP server identity, scope and authentication
entries.role: Whether a client can tell which server answered and what it is allowed to do. The protocol is young and the deployment is usually a local process with no authentication at all.
preconditions: an agent connects to one or more MCP servers
oracle: a request served by a server other than the one intended
a connection established with no verification in either direction
a server reachable from another host on the network rather than loopback only

tree.why: The attack surface is the tool registry. Everything else is an input channel into it.

next.q: Are tool descriptions pinned or fetched fresh?

branches.action: the description is attacker influenceable if any server is compromised or added. scan for injection in descriptions and diff against a known good
test the pinning itself: can a server change its description and be accepted
treat skill files as code. review what they instruct the agent to do, and whether they can read secrets or call tools
branches.oracle: skill causing an action outside its stated purpose

branches.action: enumerate arguments, then attempt to reach a state changing function with attacker controlled arguments
branches.oracle: state change from an induced call

mirror.control: pin and review descriptions, treat as code

gaps.gap: No tool diffs an MCP tool registry over time and flags description drift
gaps.build_candidate: hash every tool name, description and schema per server, store, diff on each start, report
